raid_warning: Smoke over the hills toward {other_settlement}. Bar your door tonight.
A shepherd from {other_settlement} says riders were seen {days} days back, heading this way.
The dogs have barked at the treeline every night this week. Something's out there.
They say {other_realm} is gathering spears near the border. Keep your bow strung.
Crops trampled flat in straight lines east of {settlement}. That's Forsworn work, mark me.
A pedlar was asking how many keep the walls. Never saw him buy a thing.
Raiders hit a farm near {other_settlement}. Took the {item} and the cattle, left the old folk crying.
bandit_camp: There's a bandit camp in the woods past {other_settlement}. Three carts gone this month.
Outlaws on the road to {other_settlement}. Travel in company or not at all.
My cousin was robbed of his {item} not {days} days ago. Masked folk, laughing.
Skrell or men, nobody knows, but someone's been raiding the stores at night.
The Wardens of the Road have given up on the west road. Bandits own it now.
They say the bandits are unpaid soldiers from {other_realm}. Desperate men are the worst kind.
If someone cleared out that camp, {settlement} would owe them a feast.
death: Did you hear? {person} has passed. We'll keep the candle lit.
{person} is gone. Took ill and never woke. The whole street turned out.
We buried {person} {days} days ago. Say their name if you pass the yard.
{person} died, poor soul. No kin left to tend the grave, they say. That's how the cold ones start.
They found {person} on the road outside {settlement}. No marks. Just cold.
{person} has gone back to the roots. The sapling's already in.
Grief in {settlement} today. {person} was well loved.
marriage: {person} is to be wed! The whole of {settlement} is invited, or so they say.
There's to be a wedding. {person} has found someone at last.
Did you hear? {person} married into a family from {other_settlement}. Two hearths into one.
The lot came up favourable and {person} is wed. The ancestors approve, apparently.
{person} and their sweetheart planted a marriage-tree by the well. Lovely thing.
A match between {realm} and {other_realm}, they say. Sealed with a wedding and a lot of ale.
{person} is wed. Mind you, their birth-charts didn't agree. Paid the Watchers to look again.
birth: {person} has had a baby! Healthy and loud, by all accounts.
There's a new child in {settlement}. The Flamekeeper's added a name to the roll.
{person} is a parent now. Born under a clear sky, which the Watchers like.
A baby, born in {settlement} {days} days ago. They named it after a grandparent.
New life at {person}'s house. Good. We need more of it.
The child came while the stars were falling. Omen-born, the old women say.
{person}'s little one has arrived. Ask for a slice of the naming-cake, they're handing it out.
building: They're building a new {item} in {settlement}. Hammering all day.
{settlement} has finished its new walls. Took them all summer.
{person} is raising a house by the mill. Good timber too.
Masons from {other_settlement} came to build the Kindlehall. Fine work.
They've raised a new tower at {settlement}. Lords do love a tower.
The bridge to {other_settlement} is mended at last. Trade will pick up.
Builders want paying in bread these days. Grain's that dear.
war: {realm} has declared war on {other_realm}. The levies march in {days} days.
War. Again. My boy's been called to the banners.
{other_realm} burned the fields near {other_settlement}. There'll be blood for that.
Every smith in {settlement} is making spearheads. The price of {item} has doubled.
The Ashborn companies are hiring out to {realm}. Costly, but they win.
Soldiers passed through and ate us bare. Whose side are they on? Their own stomachs.
They say the war's over a dead lord's inheritance. Thousands to die for one chair.
peace: Peace between {realm} and {other_realm}! Signed on Moot-day, so they say.
The war's over. My boy's coming home, if he's still walking.
{realm} and {other_realm} have made terms. Hostages swapped, a wedding promised.
The roads are open again. First caravan from {other_settlement} came in this morning.
Peace, for now. Plant while you can, I say.
The lords have shaken hands. We'll see how long that lasts.
They're holding a feast in {settlement} for the peace. Free ale, if you're quick.
shortage: There's no {item} to be had in {settlement}. Not for love nor money.
Grain's dear and getting dearer. Grey ear in the fields, they say.
The Honey Lane's cut. Candles are three times the price. How will the poor light their graves?
No {item} came in this week. Caravans are late, or taken.
We'll be eating acorns by Deepnight if the stores don't hold.
Someone's been buying up all the {item}. Hoarders, or worse.
{settlement} opened the Common Pot early. Things are that bad.
ruler_death: The ruler of {realm} is dead. The bells rang all night.
{person} is dead, and {realm} has no clear heir. Trouble's coming.
They say {person} was poisoned. Nobody says it loudly.
Our lord {person} has gone to the ancestors. The hall will read the name tonight.
{person} fell in battle. A good death, the soldiers say. Small comfort to the rest of us.
Mourning in {realm}. Black banners on every gate.
{person} died in their sleep. Peaceful, they say. Rare, for a ruler.
succession: {person} has taken the throne of {realm}. Long may they reign, or long enough.
The lords acclaimed {person} at the crown-moot. Not everyone cheered.
{person} holds {realm} now. The old ruler's cousins are sulking in their castles.
The ancestor-lot fell on {person}. The clans accept it. Mostly.
{person} has been confirmed sun-touched. The priests smiled. That smile cost something.
There are two claimants to {realm}. Pick a side, or keep your head down.
{person} took the Rattle and held it three days! Long live the Rattle-King, until someone steals it.
dragon_sighting: Goats came down off the peaks in daylight. My gran says that means a wyrm is waking.
Something huge flew over {other_settlement} {days} days ago. Blotted out the moon.
The hot springs are boiling and there's sulphur on the wind. Cindermaw stirs, mark me.
Frost in high summer near {other_settlement}. That's white wyrm weather.
Burnt hay and no lightning. Drakes, taking sheep from the high fields.
{realm} is talking of paying tribute to the wyrm. Shameful, but cheaper than burying people.
A knight from {settlement} rode out to hunt the wyrm. We'll know soon whether we need a new knight.
long_night: Stars fell three nights running. The Watchers have gone white as milk.
The nights are longer. Don't tell me they aren't. I've been counting candles.
The Tall Ones were seen in daylight near {settlement}. That's never good.
Graves opened in {other_settlement}. The unremembered ones. They walked.
Can't sleep either? Nobody can. Shut your shutters, the mares are thick tonight.
A quiet stranger is feeding folk by the old chapel. Asks nothing. I don't trust kindness that cheap.
The sun-priests swore the twin dawn would come. It hasn't. Folk are drifting from the temples.
refugees: Folk from {other_settlement} are on the road. Blight took their fields.
Refugees at the gate. The Flamekeeper says Bowl-Right. The reeve says the stores won't stretch.
Whole families walking out of {other_realm}. War, or hunger, or both.
{person} took in a family from the south. Hearth-kind, that one.
The camp outside {settlement} grows every day. Somebody will have to decide something.
They say {other_settlement} shut its gates on the hungry. The Grovewardens won't bless them now.
Some of the newcomers are good with a plough. Others are just hungry. Most are both.
trade: A caravan from {other_settlement} came in loaded with {item}. Prices dropped by half.
The Tidefolk want {item}, and they'll pay in silver. Good time to sell.
{settlement} is buying all the {item} it can get. Someone knows something.
Trade's good on the Kingsway this month. The Wardens have cleared the road.
Burrowfolk waggons came through with honey and candles. I bought a year's worth.
There's a skrell night-market down by the river. Good prices, no questions. Keep your purse close.
{realm} has raised its tolls. Merchants are grumbling and taking the long road.
